articles.title: IBM details major chip breakthrough with new sub-1nm 'nanostack' 3D architecture
articles.body:
IBM claims to have achieved a major chip breakthrough with the introduction of the world's first sub-1nm semiconductor technology. The company announced the 'nanostack' 3D architecture, which features an 'evolutionary transistor architecture at the 0.7 nm, or 7 angstrom node,' positioned to advance the semiconductor industry over the next decade.

The sub-1nm chips demonstrate nearly twice the density of IBM's 2nm chips from 2021, containing 100 billion transistors. These chips offer up to 50 percent greater performance or 70 percent improved energy efficiency for generative AI and cloud applications.

IBM describes the nanostack transistor architecture as the industry's first known three-dimensional, nanosheet-based design. It works by vertically stacking and staggering transistors while utilizing different material combinations in each layer to independently optimize performance and power efficiency.

The company validated the architecture through ultra-thin dielectric bonding in CMOS integration, dual-channel engineering capability demonstrations, and functional CMOS inverter operation with anticipated switching performance.

IBM developed this technology at its chip research facility in Albany, New York, which will soon house ASML's High Numerical Aperture Extreme Ultraviolet (High NA EUV) lithography equipment.

Jay Gambetta, director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow, stated the breakthrough 'marks a landmark moment in computing, pushing technology beyond the nanometer era to the scale of atoms,' emphasizing how the company is 'reinventing how chips are built to deliver dramatically more power and energy efficiency.'

Nanostack represents an industry-first three-dimensional, nanosheet-based transistor architecture. Key features include vertically stacked and staggered transistor arrangement, 3D sequential integration enabling higher transistor density, variable material combinations within each stacked layer for independent transistor optimization, dual-channel engineering capability with functional CMOS inverter operation, and ultra-thin dielectric bonding in CMOS integration.

IBM projects at least a decade of future scaling, with potential production adoption within 5 years. Performance improvements: up to 50% more performance, 70% greater energy efficiency, and 40% SRAM scaling improvement versus 2nm node chips.

articles.title: IBM Outlines Sub-1nm Nanostack Transistor Technology: Building the Next Gen By Going Up
articles.body:
IBM Research has announced a next-generation transistor design called Nanostack, targeted at sub-1nm geometries, specifically the 7 Angstrom generation. The technology uses wafer stacking to build circuits vertically rather than continuing to shrink horizontally.

While Moore's Law progress has slowed—from shrinking transistors by 50% every two years to approximately every five years—research into novel manufacturing approaches continues. Current industry leaders TSMC, Intel, and Samsung are transitioning from FinFET to Gate-All-Around (GAAFET) transistors, but these too have limited scalability. According to the piece, 'GAAFET will run its course in the early-to-mid 2030s,' making development of successor technologies urgent.

Nanostack represents IBM's proposed solution by stacking circuit components vertically. This approach aims to enable reliable manufacturing of smaller circuits while allowing further density improvements through additional layers. The technology is positioned as foundational for chip manufacturing throughout the 2030s.

The nanostack design features: nearly 100 billion transistors on a fingernail-sized chip, nearly double the density of IBM's 2nm chip from 2021. Performance metrics include up to 50% more performance than 2nm node chips, 70% greater energy efficiency than 2nm node chips, and 40% scaling improvement in SRAM technology.

articles.title: OpenAI: "New bet" to partner with semiconductor companies, using AI to optimize chip design
articles.body:
OpenAI is recruiting a deal lead to establish partnerships with semiconductor firms, leveraging its AI models for chip development and operational improvements. This hiring initiative, part of OpenAI's Special Situations team, represents a new vertical expansion.

The role focuses on identifying where AI can deliver significant value to semiconductor companies and their partners. The job listing describes these efforts as 'new bets' that may 'mature into repeatable ways of working.'

Partnership structures are expected to include 'non-standard partnerships, including revenue share, royalties, and bespoke commercial terms.' While resulting chips could potentially be used by OpenAI, this outcome isn't mandatory.

This push into chip AI automation follows OpenAI's unveiling of Jalapeño, an intelligence processor co-designed with Broadcom. The inference chip utilized OpenAI's models to accelerate design and optimization phases.

Google has similarly deployed DeepMind's AlphaChip across multiple generations of its Tensor Processing Units and Axion CPUs. Two AlphaChip creators subsequently founded Ricursive Intelligence, an independent AI chip design platform valued at $4 billion as of January 2026.

articles.title: Qualcomm unveils three new data center solutions including Dragonfly C1000 CPU, set to be deployed by Meta
articles.body:
Qualcomm has announced three new data center offerings: the Dragonfly C1000 CPU, Qualcomm High Bandwidth Compute (HBC), and the Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator. The company has entered into a multi-year partnership with Meta to deploy the C1000 CPU in Meta's next-generation server infrastructure.

The Dragonfly C1000 is a purpose-built data center processor featuring custom Oryon CPU cores optimized for 'agentic, general-purpose, and AI head node workloads.' With a 250+ core-count chiplet design, it delivers '2x better performance per watt compared to existing product benchmarks for server CPU' and is expected to launch commercially in 2028.

The Dragonfly AI300 is Qualcomm's third-generation inference accelerator offering both air and direct-liquid cooling at the rack level. It integrates HBC Gen 2 technology and is designed to provide '4x-8x better performance-per-watt compared to existing GPU-based architectures.' Commercial sampling is targeted for 2028.

The High Bandwidth Compute uses a 3D-stacked silicon architecture to address AI's data movement challenges. The AI250 with HBC Gen 1 is expected to deliver commercial sampling in mid-2027, while the AI300 with HBC Gen 2 provides a significant increase in effective memory bandwidth over prior generations.

Qualcomm CEO Christiano Amon emphasized three dimensions to the company's future, with 'rack-scale data center infrastructure' as the first priority. The company doubled its FY29 revenue forecast from $22B to $40B ($61조원), with data center becoming a major growth driver projecting over 5% of a $1 trillion-plus market within 5-7 years.

Qualcomm also announced the acquisition of AI software startup Modular for approximately $3.92 billion ($5.8조원) in an all-stock deal, aimed at creating a competitive alternative to NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem. Modular builds the Mojo programming language and the MAX inference engine, supporting chips from Nvidia, AMD, Arm, and custom ASICs without rewriting code for each platform.

Over 35 global technology companies support the Dragonfly ecosystem, including Samsung, SK Hynix, Lenovo, Foxconn, and Supermicro.

articles.title: Meta and Microsoft add more than $120bn in future lease commitments in latest quarter
articles.body:
Microsoft and Meta have signed approximately $120 billion in future capacity lease agreements during the most recent quarter, according to regulatory filings cited by Bloomberg. This brings total lease commitments among major cloud computing providers to exceed $850 billion.

Meta led with $79 billion in new commitments, representing a 76 percent increase from the previous quarter, bringing its total to $182.9 billion for the quarter ending March 31. Microsoft added $41 billion, reaching a total of $196.6 billion.

Both companies continue investing heavily in self-built and operated data centers. Meta estimates between $120 billion and $135 billion ($182조~$204조원) in capital expenditures for 2026, while Microsoft expects $190 billion ($286조원) for fiscal year 2026, with $25 billion tied to component pricing.

Recent Microsoft lease agreements include 'securing 30,000 GPUs from an Nscale data center in Norway' and a 900MW capacity deal with Crusoe for its Abilene, Texas campus. Both contracts were previously allocated to OpenAI.

In the prior quarter, both companies committed roughly $50 billion each in future leases. Currently, total commitments across Oracle, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Google, and CoreWeave reached $700 billion that quarter.

Amazon added $10 billion in the latest quarter—half its previous quarter—while Oracle's commitments decreased slightly from $261 billion to $260 billion.

articles.title: Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders introduce AI Data Center Moratorium Act
articles.body:
Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have unveiled legislation to halt data center construction. The 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Moratorium Act' targets facilities consuming over 20MW with high-density racks and liquid cooling used for large-scale AI development.

The bill would suspend new construction until federal regulations are established. Required regulations include government review of AI products before release, policies protecting jobs, equitable wealth distribution, and proof that projects won't increase utility costs or harm the climate.

The proposal grants communities veto power over projects, prohibits government subsidies, and mandates unionized labor. The Secretary of Energy would submit quarterly reports tracking water usage, energy consumption, emissions, wastewater discharge, and noise levels.

Sanders stated: 'Congress is way behind where it should be in understanding the nature of this revolution and its impacts.' He emphasized the need for 'serious public debate and democratic oversight.'

Nine House members co-sponsor the bill. The legislation notes over 100 communities and 12 states have already enacted their own data center moratoriums, though federal passage remains unlikely. The bill cites concerns from tech leaders about job displacement and AI risks.

articles.title: AWS and Microsoft designated 'gatekeepers' under Europe's Digital Markets Act
articles.body:
The European Commission has designated Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure as gatekeepers under the Digital Markets Act, despite these cloud services not meeting the DMA's quantitative thresholds for designation.

The commission's preliminary findings note that both companies 'have achieved significant turnover, and their operational capacity and investments seem to have significantly outpaced those of competitors.' Additionally, they maintain 'vast and entrenched user bases' with lock-in effects and high switching costs, plus expansive ecosystems.

The EC highlighted that AI services have become crucial in cloud procurement decisions. The agency stated that 'AI is significantly increasing the demand for cloud-related services' and both providers retain substantial market share within this growing sector.

An investigation into EU cloud service providers launched in November 2025 preceded this preliminary designation. The current findings don't prejudice the investigation's outcome.

Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice President for tech sovereignty, emphasized that 'cloud services have become a cornerstone of Europe's economy,' requiring fair and competitive markets.

AWS responded that the Commission's findings 'disregard the breadth of cloud services available to European customers' and risk deterring investment. The company argued existing regulations already govern cloud services comprehensively.

Should the findings be confirmed, both companies would have six months to comply with DMA obligations for their cloud computing services.

articles.title: Gorilla Technology secures $2.5bn GPUaaS contract in Indonesia
articles.body:
Gorilla Technology Group has secured a five-year AI compute contract valued at $2.5 billion (3조8천억원) with an unnamed customer. The contract will deploy GPUs at NeutraDC's Batam data center in Indonesia.

The initial phase includes 1,000 B300 GPU servers generating $1.3 billion (1조9천억원) in revenue over five years, with deployment targeted for September 2026, followed by a second phase in December 2026. Remaining capacity will be deployed in the first half of 2027.

The customer is described as a 'high investment-grade global technology customer' but remains unidentified. CEO Jay Chandan stated: 'This contract is a major validation of that strategy. This is not a pipeline story.'

Gorilla secured debt financing covering approximately 70 percent of expected project costs. The company signed a capacity agreement with NeutraDC in May 2026 for 5.5MW of capacity at the Batam facility located at Kabil Industrial Estate.

Previously, Gorilla signed a $1.4 billion three-year contract with Singaporean cloud provider Freyr and an April 2026 agreement with India's Yotta to deploy over 25,000 GPUs. The company is also planning a 200MW data center development in Thailand.

articles.title: The White House is asking OpenAI to slow roll the release of its new model over safety concerns
articles.body:
OpenAI plans a restricted release of GPT 5.6, sharing it only with select partners rather than the general public, following pressure from the Trump administration. During a staff meeting, CEO Sam Altman indicated that 'the government would be approving access customer by customer' during a preview phase, with hopes for broader availability 'a couple of weeks later.'

The Office of the National Cyber Director and Office of Science and Technology Policy requested the limited rollout. OpenAI staff reportedly collaborated closely with government agencies on the release strategy.

This represents a shift from the Trump administration's earlier 'hands-off' position on AI. In June, Trump signed an executive order requiring certain AI companies to voluntarily submit new models for government testing before public release.

The approach mirrors Anthropic's strategy with Claude Mythos, its frontier cyber model released only through Project Glasswing to select partners. Anthropic cited safety concerns, arguing the model's power posed misuse risks. However, observers debate whether such restrictions represent genuine safety measures or marketing tactics.

Frontier cyber tools raise legitimate concerns: generative AI can write malware and execute ransomware attacks autonomously. These models excel at identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities faster than human analysts, threatening organizations relying on complex software infrastructure.

articles.title: Databricks' former AI chief thinks he can cut AI's power bill by 1,000x
articles.body:
Naveen Rao, the former head of AI at Databricks, has launched Unconventional AI with an ambitious goal: dramatically reducing the power consumption required for AI inference processing. The company unveiled its first model, Un-0, an image-generation system that demonstrates how their oscillator-based computing architecture can match the performance of conventional AI systems like Stable Diffusion.

The breakthrough centers on a fundamentally different approach to computer architecture. Rather than relying on traditional chips powering contemporary AI systems, Unconventional AI's design uses oscillators to achieve what Rao claims could be a 1,000-fold reduction in energy consumption. 'This is the hello world of a new kind of computer,' Rao explained.

Currently, Un-0 runs on software simulations of the proposed oscillator chips. The company plans to release actual chip schematics soon and eventually build a complete inference stack, positioning itself as a compute provider operating at a fraction of typical power requirements.

Rao emphasizes that energy limitations will become the critical constraint for AI scaling. With fewer than 50 employees, Unconventional AI is tackling what may be one of the sector's most pressing challenges: 'AI scaling is hard because of energy. It's going to be the fundamental limit in the next few years.'

articles.title: Amazon ups India bet with fresh $13B AI infrastructure investment
articles.body:
Amazon announced an additional $13 billion (19조8천억원) investment in India through 2030, focusing on expanding Amazon Web Services' data center capacity in Mumbai and Hyderabad. This follows CEO Andy Jassy's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi.

The company's cumulative commitment to India now reaches $48 billion (73조원) across multiple announcements since 2023. Amazon is also expanding its domestic retail operations, planning over 20 new fulfillment centers and 100 last-mile delivery stations this year, plus extending its quick-commerce service Amazon Now to more than 300 cities.

The investment reflects intensifying competition among global tech giants betting on India as a major AI infrastructure hub. Microsoft committed $17.5 billion by 2029, while Google pledged $15 billion for AI infrastructure. Domestic players like Reliance Industries and Adani Group, plus international investors like AirTrunk and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, are similarly expanding data center projects in the country.

India has sweetened the deal with policy incentives, including tax exemptions through 2047 for foreign cloud providers offering overseas services from Indian data centers.

articles.title: A Deep Dive On China's 'LineShine' All-CPU, Exaflops-Class Supercomputer
articles.body:
China's NSC Shenzhen has unveiled LineShine, an all-CPU exascale supercomputer now ranked first on the Top500 list. The system utilizes the LingKun LX2 processor, an Armv9.2-based CPU designed collaboratively by NSC Shenzhen and Huawei's HiSilicon division.

The LX2 processor features 304 active cores per socket, incorporating SVE2 vector units and SME matrix math units. With 13.79 million cores total, LineShine achieves a peak theoretical performance of 2.74 exaflops and delivers approximately 2.2 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack benchmark—21.5 percent more powerful than the previous top-ranked 'El Capitan' system.

The architecture consists of two chiplets per CPU, likely manufactured using SMIC's 7-nanometer process at N+3 refinement, operating at 1.55 GHz. Each socket includes 64 GB of HBM memory with 8 TB/sec bandwidth and 256 GB of DRAM across eight NUMA domains.

The full LineShine configuration contains 22,680 nodes with 13.79 million cores, consuming 42.2 megawatts and achieving 80.35 percent computational efficiency. The system employs the proprietary LingQi interconnect in a dual-plane, multi-rail fat-tree topology, delivering 1.6 Tb/sec bandwidth per node.

China developed this indigenous supercomputer independently, reflecting national policies prioritizing technological self-sufficiency amid U.S. export restrictions on semiconductor technology. This is a significant milestone: the world's most powerful supercomputer uses no Nvidia, AMD, or Intel components.

articles.title: Chinese supercomputer using local processors heads TOP500 list
articles.body:
China's LineShine supercomputer has claimed the top position on the TOP500 list with a performance of 2.198 Exaflop/s, marking a significant achievement in independent processor development. The machine, housed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, operates 'without using any kit from Nvidia, Intel, or AMD.'

The system comprises 20,480 computing nodes powered by LX2 processors that 'integrate two compute dies (304 cores total) and eight on-package HBM stacks (32 GB, 4 TB/s aggregate bandwidth).' Each processor delivers 'up to 60.3/120.6 TFLOPS in FP64/FP32' performance.

The supercomputer achieved approximately 80 percent of its theoretical 2.736 Exaflop/s peak during testing and operates on KylinOS, a Linux-based distribution. Nodes connect via the LingQi high-speed network, also developed domestically in China.

This accomplishment reflects Beijing's policy push toward technological self-sufficiency. While LineShine uses ARM-based architecture (a British design), it demonstrates China's ability to develop competitive alternatives to Western processors, particularly as its nascent GPU industry continues developing capabilities that currently 'trail Nvidia and AMD by four or five years.'

articles.title: Cerebras stock plunges after earnings as CEO says margin outlook was misunderstood
articles.body:
Cerebras Systems' stock dropped nearly 20% on Wednesday following its first earnings report as a public company. Despite delivering better-than-expected Q1 results, the company's margin guidance spooked investors.

The AI chipmaker projected a full-year gross margin of 38-41%, significantly lower than the 47% achieved in Q1. This forecast caused shares to approach their IPO price, hitting new lows.

CEO Andrew Feldman explained to CNBC that 'investors had misunderstood the company's margin guidance.' The margin compression stems from a strategic decision: Cerebras will temporarily lease back some of its own systems from a major customer while constructing its own data center capacity. This arrangement prioritizes near-term capacity availability over profitability.

Financial highlights from Q1 show revenue reached $193 million (2940억원), representing 94% year-over-year growth. The company's net loss narrowed to $14 million from $23.9 million in the prior year period.

During the earnings call, management detailed how the equipment rental strategy would temporarily impact profit margins throughout the year.

articles.title: Samsung Opens ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex Access After AI Restrictions
articles.body:
Samsung Electronics has expanded employee access to OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex tools across all Korean staff and Device eXperience division employees worldwide. This represents a significant shift from the company's 2023 restrictions on generative AI use due to data security concerns.

The deployment enables staff to leverage these tools across multiple business functions including software development, marketing, product development, and manufacturing. ChatGPT Enterprise provides organizational controls for data protection and security management, addressing Samsung's earlier concerns about sensitive information being uploaded to external platforms.

The rollout covers both technical and non-technical teams, with Codex supporting code-related work alongside general workflow automation. OpenAI reports that Codex now has over five million weekly active users, with Korean usage growing nearly 800% since February 2026.

Samsung has deepened ties with OpenAI through multiple initiatives. In October 2025, the companies announced a memory partnership for OpenAI's Stargate infrastructure project, with Samsung and SK Hynix expected to supply significant portions of the 900,000 monthly DRAM wafers needed. Samsung SDS also secured reseller agreements to offer OpenAI services in Korea.

Research from Deloitte's 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise found that 66% of organizations reported productivity gains from enterprise AI adoption.

articles.title: AMD And Nvidia Are Neck And Neck In HPC Supercomputing
articles.body:
The article analyzes the competitive landscape between AMD and NVIDIA in high-performance computing based on the June 2026 Top500 supercomputer rankings.

NVIDIA dominates in quantity with 237 accelerated systems versus AMD's 32 systems on the Top500 list. The competition tightens considerably when measuring actual computational capacity. AMD operates 8.18 exaflops of installed capacity compared to Nvidia's 11 exaflops. Additionally, AMD has sold accelerated machines with a combined CPU and GPU concurrency of 35.3 million cores compared to Nvidia's 38.9 million cores.

New installations reveal preference patterns. Many HPC centers continue selecting NVIDIA's older Hopper GPUs over newer Blackwell models due to cost and performance advantages. There are also a lot of clusters that have Intel Xeon processors married to Nvidia GPUs, reflecting CPU preferences and availability constraints during the AI boom.

The author characterizes this as 'a real race,' suggesting AMD's competitive position in accelerated HPC computing may foreshadow similar dynamics in AI infrastructure markets.

articles.title: [데이터뉴스]2026년 반도체 장비 투자 50% 이상 급증…웨이퍼 전공정 장비 강세
articles.body:
글로벌 반도체 제조 장비 투자 규모가 인공지능(AI) 수요 폭증에 힘입어 2026년 본격적인 확대 국면에 들어선 것으로 나타났다.

시장조사업체 테크인사이츠(TechInsights)가 최근 발간한 '2026 Semiconductor Outlook Report'에 따르면, '2026년 반도체 장비 지출이 2025년 대비 50% 이상 증가할 전망'이다.

특히 2026년 4분기에는 전체 장비 지출이 605억 달러(약 8조3000억원)에 달해 사상 최고치를 기록할 것으로 예상된다. 2025년 1분기 399억달러였던 전체 장비 지출은 2026년 4분기 이르러 약 51.6% 증가할 것으로 전망된다.

장비 지출 비중과 증가분 모두 웨이퍼 전공정 장비(WFE)가 가장 큰 비중을 차지하고 있다. 2026년 4분기 WFE 지출은 427억달러로 전체의 약 70%를 차지하며, 절대액 기준으로도 3분기 만에 145억달러가 늘어났다. AI 관련 첨단 공정 투자 확대를 선명하게 보여주고 있다.

테스트 및 관련 장비는 2026년 4분기 114억달러, 서비스 및 지원 부문은 48억달러, 후공정·패키징 장비는 16억달러로 각각 집계됐다. 2025년 내내 분기당 380~430억 달러 수준에서 비교적 안정적으로 유지되던 장비 지출이 2026년 들어 급격한 상승 곡선을 그리고 있는 것이다. 특히 2026년 상반기부터 뚜렷한 증가세를 보이며 하반기에 투자 피크를 형성할 것으로 보인다.

보고서는 AI 수요가 지속되면서 HBM4 메모리, 2나노 게이트올어라운드(GAA) 공정, 어드밴스드 패키징 수요가 폭발적으로 늘어나고 있다고 분석했다.

특히 HBM4는 2026년 16단 제품 양산이 시작되면서 메모리 시장 회복과 함께 전공정 장비 수요를 직접적으로 자극할 것으로 봤다. 실리콘포토닉스(CPO) 등 첨단 패키징 기술이 AI 서버의 전력 문제를 해결하는 핵심 솔루션으로 부상하면서 관련 장비 투자도 함께 늘어나고 있다고 전망했다.

articles.title: TSMC Clients Handed Price Hikes Across All Advanced Nodes
articles.body:
TSMC is implementing price increases across its entire advanced node portfolio—7nm and beyond—affecting approximately 75% of the company's wafer revenue base. This represents a significantly broader impact than previously expected by industry observers.

The foundry has instructed sales teams to raise prices across all advanced nodes, not just the 3nm process as earlier rumors suggested. The 3nm node alone represented 25% of wafer revenue in Q1 2026, but the comprehensive price hike extends to legacy nodes as well.

Price increases appear to fall between 5-10%, though exact figures vary by client, node type, and product category. Implementation has already begun, with customers directed to incorporate higher costs into purchase orders.

Chairman CC Wei indicated he would 'like to' raise prices, while CFO Wendell Huang stated he 'does not rule out' price increases. When contacted, TSMC responded: 'TSMC does not comment on pricing. Our pricing strategy is strategic, not opportunistic.'

A 5% average increase could boost full-year gross margin by 2+ percentage points, potentially affecting approximately $70 billion in advanced-node sales during the second half of 2026. Major affected customers include Nvidia, AMD, Apple, Qualcomm, and Broadcom, all of which depend heavily on TSMC's leading-edge processes.

articles.title: Rebellions, CCK Solution Partner on Enterprise AI Transformation Infrastructure
articles.body:
AI chip startup Rebellions has partnered with CCK Solution, an AI workflow automation provider, through a strategic memorandum of understanding aimed at supporting enterprise AI transformation initiatives.

The partnership focuses on delivering agentic AI solutions for back-office automation in accounting and administrative operations. Both companies plan to develop infrastructure that enhances efficiency of agentic AI systems while managing token consumption, offering integrated services ready for immediate deployment.

Collaboration models under consideration include supplying Rebellions' AI chips for CCK Solution's server platforms, offering Neural Processing Unit-as-a-Service solutions via cloud partnerships, or deploying dedicated AI server infrastructure within customer data centers. Specific processors and final infrastructure details remain undetermined.

Rebellions offers low-power, high-performance server-grade NPUs, including Atom and Rebel product families. Its second-generation Rebel-100 NPU is in mass production with customer shipments expected in the second half of 2026.

Park Sung-hyun, Rebellions CEO, stated: 'We will work with CCK Solution to respond to increasing AX demand in government and enterprise markets.'

CCK Solution CEO Cho Hyun-soo emphasized creating an ecosystem delivering measurable business outcomes through their AI work-platform technologies.

articles.title: Rebellions, CCK Solution team up to build Korean AI ecosystem
articles.body:
Rebellions announced a strategic partnership with CCK Solution to develop a comprehensive Korean artificial intelligence ecosystem. The collaboration merges Rebellions' energy-efficient, high-performance neural processing unit technology with CCK Solution's AI work platform.

The joint initiative focuses on creating an integrated solution enabling immediate corporate deployment without requiring separate infrastructure investment. This approach aims to streamline the deployment complexity enterprises typically encounter and reduce token usage expenses.

CCK Solution specializes in automating back-office operations through a platform that breaks down complex business processes into modular components, managed by intelligent AI agents. The company currently serves major South Korean accounting firms while expanding into broader commercial and governmental sectors.

Rebellions' CEO stated that 'a Korean AI ecosystem is completed when capable companies in hardware and software closely cooperate.' He emphasized their combined approach would address market demand for AX transformation across private and public sectors.

CCK Solution's CEO reiterated similar sentiments, noting their partnership demonstrates 'the true competitiveness of a Korean AI full stack.'

articles.title: "모델이 하네스를 먹어 치울 것"...구글이 본 AI 경쟁의 다음 단계
articles.body:
AI 업계는 지난 2년 동안 에이전트를 새로운 경쟁의 중심으로 여겨 왔습니다. 특히, 최근에는 대형언어모델(LLM) 자체보다 이를 활용해 외부 도구를 연결하고, 여러 작업을 오케스트레이션하며, 실제 업무를 수행하는 에이전트 계층이 새로운 가치를 만들 것이라는 목소리가 커졌습니다.

하지만 구글 딥마인드의 로건 킬패트릭 AI 스튜디오 책임자는 최근 팟캐스트에서 이 같은 통념에 의문을 제기했습니다. 현재 수많은 스타트업과 개발사들이 경쟁적으로 구축하고 있는 에이전트 하네스(harness)와 스캐폴딩(scaffolding)이 결국 모델 자체에 흡수될 것이라는 전망입니다.

그는 "우리가 역사적으로 모델이라고 생각했던 것은 더 이상 단순한 모델이 아니다"라며 "이제 모델은 가중치(weights)만이 아니라, 그 가중치를 둘러싼 거대한 시스템 전체"라고 설명했습니다.

하네스는 모델과 외부 도구를 연결하고, 작업 순서를 계획하며, 여러 기능을 조율하는 일종의 제어 계층입니다. 최근 등장한 다양한 AI 코딩 에이전트와 워크플로 플랫폼, MCP 기반 서비스 등이 여기에 해당합니다.

그러나 킬패트릭은 이러한 구조가 장기적인 차별화 요소가 되기는 어렵다고 봤습니다. 그는 "지금은 모두가 하네스를 구축해야 한다고 생각하고, 그곳에 알파(alpha·차별화 가치)가 있다"며 "하지만, 12개월 뒤에도 지금과 같은 의미의 하네스가 여전히 중요할 것이라고 생각하지 않는다"라고 말했습니다.

이어 "모델이 그 기능의 상당 부분을 소화(digest)하게 될 것이며, 결국 모델 내부로 업스트림(upstream)될 것"이라며 "알파는 또 다른 곳으로 이동할 것"이라고 덧붙였습니다.

articles.title: 오픈AI, 자체 개발 '추론 칩' 공개… "9개월 만에 테이프아웃"
articles.body:
오픈AI가 브로드컴과 공동 개발한 첫 번째 자체 AI 추론 칩 '할라페뇨(Jalapeño)'를 공개했다. 9개월이라는 초단기 개발 사이클로 첨단 반도체 역사상 가장 빠른 ASIC 개발 사례로 평가받고 있다.

할라페뇨는 대형언어모델(LLM) 추론에 특화된 가속기로, TSMC 3나노 공정으로 제조되며 HBM 스택 8개를 탑재한다. 기존 GPU 대비 추론 토큰 비용을 약 50% 절감할 수 있다는 것이 오픈AI의 주장이다.

오픈AI는 자체 모델을 활용해 칩 설계 및 최적화 과정을 가속화했다고 밝혔다. 이 칩은 2026년 말 초기 배포를 시작으로 점차 확대될 예정이다.

브로드컴과 마이크로소프트, 기타 파트너사들과 함께 기가와트 규모의 데이터센터 구축을 목표로 하고 있다. 오픈AI는 '풀 스택'을 직접 구축하겠다는 전략적 의지를 다시 한 번 확인했다.

articles.title: [게시판] 메가존클라우드, NIPA 국산 AI 반도체 인프라 실증 사업 참여 등 단신
articles.body:
메가존클라우드가 한국지능정보사회진흥원(NIPA) 주관 '국산 AI 반도체 인프라 실증 사업'에 참여한다고 밝혔다. 이번 사업은 국내 AI 반도체 기업들의 인프라 실증 지원을 위한 프로젝트로, 국산 반도체 경쟁력 강화에 초점을 맞추고 있다.

메가존클라우드는 클라우드 인프라 및 AI 서비스 전문 기업으로서 사업 참여를 통해 국산 AI 반도체 상용화 및 생태계 확산을 지원할 계획이다. 사업 세부 내용과 참여 반도체 기업 명단은 추후 공개될 예정이다.

articles.title: 퀄컴, AI 데이터센터 CPU 시장 본격 진입... 메타에 '드래곤플라이 C1000' 공급
articles.body:
퀄컴이 AI 데이터센터 시장 공략을 본격화하며 스마트폰 중심 사업 구조 탈피에 속도를 내고 있다.

CNBC 등에 따르면 퀄컴은 24일(현지시간) 투자자 행사에서 데이터센터용 CPU '드래곤플라이 C1000(Dragonfly C1000)'을 공개하고, 메타가 해당 칩을 차세대 AI 인프라에 채택하기로 했다고 밝혔다.

이 칩은 에이전틱 AI 환경에 최적화된 제품으로, 높은 연산 성능과 전력 효율성을 동시에 제공하는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 메타는 오는 2028년부터 자사 데이터센터에 드래곤플라이 C1000과 후속 세대 제품을 도입할 예정이다.

이번 발표는 스마트폰 프로세서와 통신 모뎀 시장의 강자로 알려진 퀄컴이 AI 데이터센터 시장에 본격적으로 진출했음을 보여주는 신호로 평가된다. 퀄컴은 CPU뿐 아니라 AI 가속기, 다수의 칩을 연결하는 플랫폼 등 다양한 제품군을 통해 급성장하는 AI 인프라 시장을 공략하겠다는 전략을 제시했다.

크리스티아노 아몬 퀄컴 CEO는 '그동안 기술과 자산을 꾸준히 축적해 왔으며 이제 데이터센터 사업의 다음 단계로 진입할 수 있는 종합적인 포트폴리오를 갖추게 됐다'고 말했다.

퀄컴은 AI 데이터센터 사업 성장에 대한 자신감도 드러냈다. 2029 회계연도 데이터센터 매출 목표를 150억달러(약 23조원)로 제시했으며, 스마트폰 외 사업 부문 매출 목표도 기존 220억달러에서 400억달러(약 61조원)로 상향 조정했다.

퀄컴은 소프트웨어 경쟁력 강화를 위해 AI 소프트웨어 스타트업 모듈러를 약 39억2000만달러(약 5조8000억원) 규모의 주식 교환 방식으로 인수한다고 발표했다. 모듈러는 엔비디아의 CUDA와 유사하게 다양한 반도체 아키텍처에서 AI 모델을 구동할 수 있는 소프트웨어 플랫폼을 개발하는 기업이다.

퀄컴은 중국 바이트댄스와 맞춤형 칩 설계 서비스 제공을 논의 중인 것으로도 알려졌다.

articles.title: Qualcomm Unveils Dragonfly Data Center Platform, Wins Meta Deal
articles.body:
Qualcomm introduced its Dragonfly family of AI data center products alongside High Bandwidth Computing (HBC) technology during its June 24 Investor Day event. The portfolio encompasses the C1000 data center CPU, AI300 inference accelerator, custom ASICs, and connectivity solutions.

The C1000 processor, built on Qualcomm's Oryon architecture, features over 250 CPU cores operating above 5GHz using chiplet design. According to executives, it delivers 'more than twice the performance per watt of competing server CPUs.' The processor supports PCIe 7.0 and CXL connectivity, enabling data transfer rates up to 2TB/s.

HBC technology stacks LPDDR memory dies vertically above accelerator chips, creating near-memory computing architecture. Qualcomm claims HBC achieves 'six times higher bandwidth per watt than HBM' while reducing thermal output and total cost of ownership compared to HBM-based systems.

The company announced a multi-year agreement with Meta to supply Dragonfly C1000 CPUs for next-generation server deployments. Volume production begins in 2028, with Humain as the launch customer. Over 35 global technology companies support the ecosystem, including Samsung, SK hynix, Lenovo, Foxconn, and Supermicro.

articles.title: Netris raises $15M Series A from a16z to help AI neoclouds go live faster
articles.body:
Netris, a network automation startup, has secured $15 million in Series A funding from Andreessen Horowitz to accelerate AI neocloud deployment timelines.

The company provides hardware-accelerated software running on network switches to help emerging data center operators reduce time-to-market. Unlike traditional software-defined networking (SDN), Netris emphasizes that 'for AI, software is not okay, because the amount of traffic is so high, everything must be hardware accelerated,' according to CEO Alex Saroyan.

The platform automates network setup, configuration, and operations while enabling multi-tenancy isolation and hardware-agnostic vendor support. Netris is currently live across more than 35 GPU clusters globally, managing approximately one million GPUs for clients including Lightning AI, Foxconn, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

Notably, the company uses deterministic algorithms developed before the AI boom rather than machine learning. Saroyan explained that 'for changing many thousands of switch configurations, you don't need to be creative. You need to be very persistent and repeatable.'

Andreessen Horowitz partner Guido Appenzeller joins the board. The funding will support engineering and sales expansion, additional hardware vendor integration, and algorithm enhancements.

articles.title: Patronus AI lands $50M to build 'digital worlds' that stress-test AI agents
articles.body:
Patronus AI has secured $50 million to develop 'digital worlds' designed specifically to stress-test and evaluate AI agents in simulated environments that mimic real-world scenarios. The funding round was led by prominent investors in the AI evaluation space.

The company's platform creates synthetic environments where AI agents can be tested against edge cases, adversarial scenarios, and complex multi-step tasks before deployment. This addresses a critical gap in AI development: current testing methodologies often fail to reveal how agents behave in production conditions.

Patronus AI's technology is particularly relevant for enterprise customers deploying agentic AI systems in high-stakes domains such as finance, healthcare, and legal services. The startup's approach goes beyond traditional benchmarking by creating dynamic, interactive test environments that evolve as AI capabilities improve.

The $50 million investment will be used to expand the platform's coverage of industry-specific testing scenarios and to scale the company's engineering team.

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude is winning over paid consumers, a market owned by ChatGPT
articles.body:
Anthropic's Claude is gaining significant traction among paid AI subscribers, challenging ChatGPT's long-standing dominance in the consumer market. New data suggests Claude's subscription growth has accelerated dramatically in the second quarter of 2026.

Despite the Trump administration's restrictions on Anthropic's most advanced Mythos and Fable models, Claude's consumer-facing subscription service has grown substantially. The restrictions appear to have paradoxically boosted Claude's brand recognition and trust among safety-conscious users.

The competitive landscape for paid AI subscriptions has intensified, with ChatGPT, Claude, and Google's Gemini all vying for the same pool of paying customers. Claude's differentiation strategy has focused on reliability, honesty, and safety features that appeal to enterprise and professional users.

The data represents a notable shift in an AI market that has long been viewed as a two-horse race between OpenAI and Google, with Anthropic emerging as a genuine third force in the consumer segment.

articles.title: Napatech Receives First Production Order for AI Infrastructure Design Win
articles.body:
Napatech announced that it has received the first material commercial purchase order associated with a major AI infrastructure design win secured in 2025. The initial order of 1,000 units, with multi-million dollar value, marks the transition from development into commercial production.

The customer's AI Inferencing platform leverages Napatech's high performance programmable SmartNIC architecture to deliver efficient, high-throughput, low latency, scale out connectivity for distributed AI workloads. The contract supports Napatech's financial guidance for the full year of 2026, which is unchanged.

This announcement represents a significant milestone for Napatech, validating its strategy in the growing AI infrastructure market. The company's SmartNIC technology is positioned as a key connectivity solution for distributed AI inference deployments at scale.

articles.title: Micron and Anthropic Announce Strategic Agreement to Scale Next-Generation AI Infrastructure
articles.body:
Micron Technology and Anthropic announced a strategic agreement on June 22, 2026 to scale next-generation AI infrastructure. The deal covers co-design of memory and storage architecture, a multi-year supply agreement spanning Micron's full data-center portfolio, internal deployment of Claude across Micron, and a strategic investment by Micron in Anthropic's Series H funding round.

The supply agreement covers Micron's three data-center memory and storage layers: HBM (high-bandwidth memory), DRAM, and SSDs, which are the layers that underpin both AI training and inference.

All three global HBM suppliers are now Anthropic Series H partners, with Samsung and SK Hynix named at the round's close on May 28, 2026, and Micron's participation announced about 25 days later on June 22. No other AI lab has the full global HBM supply trio as strategic infrastructure investors.

Micron Technology stock hit a record closing price of $1,211.38 on June 22, 2026, after the announcement. Both companies confirmed the size of Micron's Series H investment and the supply agreement's financial terms are undisclosed.

articles.title: US memory triopolist makes its customers pay
articles.body:
Micron Technology is increasingly locking customers into long-term supply contracts as AI memory demand surges, a strategy that mirrors what South Korean rivals Samsung and SK Hynix have already adopted. The shift toward contracted volumes represents a fundamental change in how memory is bought and sold.

Micron's Q3 FY2026 earnings revealed the company is converting spot-market customers to multi-year agreements, reducing price volatility risk while securing stable revenue streams. This 'triopolist' behavior—where all three major DRAM/HBM suppliers move simultaneously to long-term contracts—could reshape procurement strategies for hyperscalers and AI hardware vendors.

The contracts typically include volume commitments across DRAM, NAND, and HBM products, with pricing indexed to market conditions but with floor protections. Customers gain supply security during the ongoing memory shortage; suppliers gain revenue predictability for their massive capital expenditure programs.

articles.title: DDN launches faster array HW and KV Cache SW for AI
articles.body:
DDN has launched new hardware and software products targeting AI inference workloads, specifically addressing the growing demand for efficient KV (key-value) cache management in large language model serving.

The new hardware array delivers significantly higher throughput for AI training and inference storage needs, while the KV Cache software optimizes how attention states are stored and retrieved during inference. As LLM context windows expand to millions of tokens, KV cache management has become a critical bottleneck affecting both latency and infrastructure costs.

DDN's solution positions the company as a key infrastructure player in the AI inference stack, competing with specialized memory solutions from NVIDIA and storage-focused AI infrastructure vendors. The KV cache software is designed to work across multiple GPU vendors and can reduce memory pressure on expensive HBM resources.

articles.title: AI chip startup Rebellions raises $400m in pre-IPO funding round, launches two AI infrastructure platforms
articles.body:
AI chip startup Rebellions has raised $400 million in a pre-IPO funding round at a $2.34 billion valuation, and launched two new AI infrastructure platforms aimed at expanding its commercial footprint beyond Korea.

The funding will support mass production of the company's Rebel-100 NPU, which is already in production with customer shipments expected in the second half of 2026. Rebellions is also pursuing a dual listing strategy targeting both KOSDAQ and Nasdaq.

The company launched two new infrastructure platforms: a rack-scale AI inference system and a cloud-native NPU-as-a-Service offering. Both platforms are built around the Rebel-100's key differentiators: lower power consumption compared to GPU alternatives and higher inference throughput per watt.

Rebellions CEO Park Sung-hyun stated the NPU era will break NVIDIA's monopoly, citing the company's benchmark results showing 5-7x better price efficiency compared to competing GPU-based systems in real-world inference deployments.

The company is expanding its Middle East presence, having recently recruited a former diplomat to lead regional business development as US-Iran tensions that previously hampered the market begin to ease.

articles.title: NVIDIA powers over 400 of the world's top 500 supercomputers — June 2026 Top500 analysis
articles.body:
The June 2026 TOP500 list has been released, revealing that NVIDIA's technologies now power more than 400 of the world's top 500 supercomputers. NVIDIA's technology runs 81% of TOP500 systems, while 90% of systems newly added to the list use NVIDIA acceleration.

NVIDIA GPU acceleration reached a record 238 systems, while NVIDIA networking reached 376 systems. This dominance is reinforced by the increasing deployment of Blackwell-generation hardware across major HPC centers.

Notably, the top position belongs to LineShine, which debuted at No. 1 with 2.198 exaflops on the HPL benchmark, displacing El Capitan. This Chinese supercomputer took the top spot without using any NVIDIA, Intel, or AMD components, using the domestically-developed LX2 ARM-based processor.

AMD shows strong representation with 191 total systems, up 11% year-over-year, and 41% of new systems in this year's list including El Capitan (No. 2) and Frontier (No. 3).

articles.title: Qualcomm acquires AI startup Modular in open ecosystem bet to challenge CUDA
articles.body:
Qualcomm is acquiring AI software firm Modular for nearly $4 billion (6조원) in an all-stock deal, representing a strategic bet to create a competitive alternative to NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem.

Modular builds the Mojo programming language and the MAX inference engine, a hardware-agnostic stack that lets developers write AI code once and run it across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and custom ASICs without rewriting for each chip. This 'write once, run anywhere' approach directly challenges CUDA's platform lock-in.

Chris Lattner, Modular's co-founder, is the legendary software engineer behind open source compiler LLVM and Apple's Swift programming language, lending significant credibility to the technical foundation.

The acquisition accelerates Qualcomm's data center strategy by providing the software layer necessary to complement its Dragonfly C1000 CPU and AI300 inference accelerator hardware. Without competitive software, hardware alternatives to NVIDIA struggle to gain enterprise adoption.

Qualcomm aims to leverage Modular's platform to support its ecosystem of 35+ data center partners, including Samsung, SK Hynix, Lenovo, Foxconn, and Supermicro. The deal is expected to close in the second half of 2026.

articles.title: The math behind the OpenAI Jalapeño chip
articles.body:
OpenAI and Broadcom's Jalapeño chip represents a bet that purpose-built silicon can dramatically reduce the cost of LLM inference compared to general-purpose GPU clusters. The economics behind the chip reveal several key design choices.

Jalapeño is built on TSMC's 3nm process node and features eight HBM memory stacks in a reticle-sized ASIC configuration—the largest die size manufacturable on a single lithography pass. This maximizes on-chip memory bandwidth, the primary bottleneck in autoregressive LLM inference.

By designing the chip specifically around the compute patterns of transformer attention and feed-forward layers, Broadcom and OpenAI claim to achieve much higher hardware utilization than GPU alternatives. GPUs are designed for flexibility; Jalapeño sacrifices generality for efficiency.

The chip's development was accelerated using OpenAI's own AI models to assist in design optimization—a recursive use of AI to build AI infrastructure. This nine-month tape-out represents what the companies describe as the fastest advanced ASIC development cycle in history.

Deployment is targeted for end of 2026, with OpenAI planning to use Jalapeño for cost-sensitive inference workloads while maintaining GPU clusters for training and latency-sensitive deployments.

articles.title: Qualcomm Investor Day 2026 Data Center Announcements CPUs, AI Accelerators, and More
articles.body:
Patrick Kennedy reports from Qualcomm's Investor Day 2026 in New York City, covering the company's data center strategy announcements.

Qualcomm CEO Christiano Amon emphasized three dimensions to the company's future, with 'rack-scale data center infrastructure' as the first priority. The company announced several major initiatives:

High Bandwidth Compute (HBC): Qualcomm introduced HBC as an alternative to traditional HBM configurations. Rather than using an interposer, the technology stacks approximately 768GB of LPDDR memory directly on compute tiles. The company claims this approach delivers superior performance-per-watt by eliminating the power overhead of interposer connections.

Dragonfly C1000 CPU: This chiplet design features 250+ cores running at 5GHz, PCIe Gen7, CXL support, and optional HBC attachment. The processor promises '2x better performance per watt' compared to competitors and includes enterprise reliability features.

Software Stack: Qualcomm acquired Modular to address longstanding software challenges. The acquisition aims to create a competitive alternative to established frameworks like CUDA.

Customer Wins: Meta entered a multi-generational agreement to use Qualcomm processors, representing a significant validation for the company's data center ambitions.

Financial Outlook: Qualcomm doubled its FY29 revenue forecast from $22B to $40B, with data center becoming a major growth driver. The company projects capturing over 5% of a $1 trillion-plus market within 5-7 years.

articles.title: OpenAI Jalapeño Intelligence Platform Shown Powered by Broadcom
articles.body:
ServeTheHome reports on OpenAI's Jalapeño intelligence processor announcement, the company's first custom AI chip co-developed with Broadcom. The platform represents OpenAI's move to build proprietary silicon infrastructure to reduce dependence on GPU suppliers.

Jalapeño is an ASIC designed specifically for LLM inference, featuring TSMC 3nm fabrication and eight HBM stacks. The chip was designed in just nine months—reportedly the fastest development cycle for an advanced AI ASIC.

Broadcom's role extends beyond manufacturing; the company contributed its expertise in custom ASIC design, which it has honed through similar partnerships with Google (TPU), Meta, Apple, and other hyperscalers.

OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño at scale by end of 2026, with Microsoft and other data center partners participating in the gigawatt-scale buildout. The chip aims to reduce inference costs by approximately 50% compared to equivalent GPU-based solutions.

This marks OpenAI's entry into the silicon supply chain, following in the footsteps of Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, all of which have developed proprietary AI chips to supplement or replace Nvidia GPU purchases.

articles.title: Arm CPUs Take Number 1 in Latest Top500 List with Chinese LineShine
articles.body:
The June 2026 Top500 supercomputer rankings feature a historic achievement: an ARM-based system has taken the number 1 position for the first time. China's LineShine, built with domestically-designed LX2 processors based on Armv9.2 architecture, delivers 2.198 exaflops on HPL, surpassing the US-based El Capitan system.

The LX2 processor, developed by the National Supercomputing Center Shenzhen in collaboration with HiSilicon, features 304 cores per CPU and on-package HBM memory providing 4 TB/s bandwidth per socket. The full system uses 22,680 nodes.

This is significant beyond the performance milestone: LineShine was built entirely without US technology—no Nvidia GPUs, no AMD processors, no Intel components. China has demonstrated it can build world-class supercomputing infrastructure using domestically developed chips despite export controls.

The LX2's manufacturing process is believed to use SMIC's most advanced N+3 7nm node, showing China's foundry capabilities approaching competitiveness with Western peers for CPU workloads (though trailing significantly for GPU/AI accelerator performance).

articles.title: HPE Delivers Upgraded HPC Hardware, Software For Security, Sovereignty, And Multi-Tenancy
articles.body:
HPE has unveiled upgraded HPC hardware and software specifically designed to address enterprise demands for security, data sovereignty, and multi-tenant AI workloads. The announcement builds on HPE's position in the datacenter AI infrastructure market following its Discover 2026 conference presentations.

The upgraded systems focus on workload isolation and secure AI compute environments, addressing concerns from government and regulated enterprise customers who require strict data sovereignty controls. Multi-tenancy capabilities allow multiple organizations to share physical infrastructure while maintaining logical separation.

HPE's approach positions the company to capture sovereign AI deployments, where governments and national enterprises are increasingly demanding that AI infrastructure remain under domestic control and within national regulatory frameworks.

articles.title: Can you really make chips in space?
articles.body:
Data Center Dynamics examines the feasibility and current state of semiconductor manufacturing in space. As terrestrial chip fabs face increasing energy, water, and geopolitical constraints, some companies are exploring whether microgravity and vacuum conditions could enable novel chip manufacturing processes.

The analysis examines proposals from several startups claiming that the absence of gravity enables the growth of more perfect crystal structures for semiconductors, potentially enabling higher performance and lower defect rates. In microgravity, convection currents that cause imperfections in crystal growth on Earth are eliminated.

However, the practical challenges are immense: launch costs, radiation environments, the need for human maintenance, and the complexity of operating precision equipment in orbit all present major hurdles. Current proposals remain largely theoretical or limited to very small-scale demonstrations.

The piece concludes that while space-based chip manufacturing is a fascinating long-term possibility, it remains decades away from commercial viability and is unlikely to address near-term semiconductor capacity constraints driven by AI demand.

articles.title: SK하이닉스, 45조 규모 미국 IPO 추진...7월10일 상장 목표
articles.body:
SK하이닉스가 대규모 미국 주식 상장에 나선다. 24일(현지시간) 블룸버그와 파이낸셜타임스 등에 따르면, SK하이닉스는 미국 증권거래위원회(SEC)에 등록 서류를 제출하고 신주 1779만주를 발행해 294억달러(약 45조4500억원)를 조달한다고 밝혔다. 7월10일 나스닥 상장이 목표다.

이번 공모는 뱅크오브아메리카, 씨티그룹, 골드만삭스, JP모건체이스 등이 주도한다. 294억달러는 지난 2019년 사우디 아람코의 기업공개 규모와 견줄 만한 규모로, 환율에 따라 역대 주식 판매량 상위 5위 안에 포함될 가능성이 있다.

FTSE 러셀의 글로벌 투자 연구 책임자인 인드라니 데는 "SK 하이닉스의 뛰어난 실적은 HBM 경쟁에서 선제적으로 나선 전략과 HBM 칩에 대한 강력한 수요를 반영한 것"이라며, 한국 기업들이 80%의 시장 점유율을 차지하며 주도권을 쥐고 있는 HBM 시장의 공급 부족이 수년간 지속될 것으로 예상된다고 설명했다.

앤트로픽과 오픈AI 등 글로벌 AI 기업이 IPO를 준비 중인 가운데, 이번 IPO는 시장 선호도를 파악하는 중요한 지표가 될 것이라는 분석이다.

articles.title: AI Is Designing Radio Chips That Humans Couldn't Even Imagine
articles.body:
IEEE Spectrum reports on a new research development in which AI systems are autonomously designing radio frequency integrated circuits with architectures that human engineers would not have conceived. The AI-generated chips demonstrate unusual topologies that challenge conventional understanding of circuit design.

The research demonstrates generative AI and reinforcement learning applied to analog and mixed-signal circuit design, a domain previously considered resistant to automation due to its reliance on human intuition and experience. The resulting circuits show competitive or superior performance metrics compared to human-designed equivalents.

This development has implications for both the semiconductor design industry and the competitive landscape for EDA (electronic design automation) tools. As AI increasingly handles lower-level design tasks, the role of human chip designers may shift toward higher-level architectural decisions and specification.

articles.title: 퀄컴·메타, 데이터센터 CPU 분야서 협력 체제 구축
articles.body:
퀄컴과 메타는 24일(현지시간) 데이터센터용 CPU 분야에서 향후 수 년간 여러 세대에 걸쳐 협력하겠다고 밝혔다. 퀄컴이 같은 날 공개한 데이터센터 전용 CPU '드래곤플라이 C1000'이 메타 차세대 서버에 탑재된다.

드래곤플라이 C1000은 5GHz 이상으로 동작하는 오라이언 코어 250개 이상을 탑재하며 PCI 익스프레스 7.0, CXL, 2TB/s 이상의 입출력 대역폭을 지원한다.

크리스티아노 아몬 퀄컴 CEO는 '대규모 데이터센터 환경을 위해 코어당 성능과 전력 효율 모두에서 혁신적인 CPU를 설계했다'며 협력의 의의를 강조했다. 그는 모바일 기기에서의 협력을 데이터센터로 확대한다고 덧붙였다.

마크 저커버그 메타 CEO는 인공지능 시대 인프라 구축이 협력의 핵심 배경이라고 설명했다. 메타는 차세대 서버에 드래곤플라이 C1000을 탑재해 각종 서비스에 활용할 예정이며, 양산은 2028년 하반기부터 시작될 예정이다.

articles.title: General Intuition's $2.3B bet that video games can train AI agents for the real world
articles.body:
General Intuition has secured $2.3 billion in funding to develop technology that uses video game environments as training grounds for AI agents that will eventually operate in the physical world. The company argues that game engines provide the richest available source of diverse, interactive, physics-accurate simulation data.

The approach leverages the massive library of existing game environments and the ability to generate novel scenarios at scale, enabling AI agents to encounter edge cases and develop robust decision-making that generalizes to real-world deployment.

This is one of the largest single funding rounds in AI infrastructure and training methodology, reflecting growing investor conviction that synthetic training environments are the path to reliable agentic AI. The funding will be used to expand the simulation infrastructure and develop partnerships with game engine providers.
